Subject: Token routing fallthrough impacting US-WEST routes (status and next steps)

Hi Elena / Novaflow ops team,

Quick heads-up — we’ve detected a routing fallthrough condition affecting a subset of US-WEST inference routes that hit our fallback pool and triggered transient token-level throttling. This has manifested as elevated p95 latency and occasional 502/503 responses for some requests between ~08:50–09:05 PDT.

What we know so far:
- Root symptom: requests intended for dedicated routing were routed to the shared fallback pool due to an intermediate routing cache miss after a config sync.
- Impact: ~3% of Novaflow’s requests in the US-WEST region experienced elevated p95 (2.3s -> 4.7s) and sporadic 502s. No data loss reported.
- Mitigation in progress: we temporarily increased capacity on the fallback pool and adjusted the routing policy to prefer hot-path pinning for active sessions.

Immediate next steps we are executing now (ETA 30–45 mins):
1) roll-forward a routing-cache patch to prevent repeated cache-miss fallthroughs;
2) scale fallback capacity by +30% for US-WEST;
3) run a short smoke test and confirm recovery metrics.

We’ve opened a dedicated incident page with live metrics: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RC-2026-10-27-1
I’m attaching the short connection logs we pulled from 08:45–09:10 for your ops team to review.

[attachment: logs-20261027.txt (text/plain, 412KB)]

I’ll send a follow-up with a concise timeline and the post-incident summary once we have the root cause validated. Apologies for the disruption — we know low latency is critical for Novaflow’s production traffic.

—Marcus

Subject: Post-incident summary: token routing fallthrough — Novaflow (RC-2026-10-27-1)

Elena — attaching the brief post-incident summary we promised. Key points below.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause: a rare race during config sync caused the routing cache to fail to mark active session routes as hot, creating a fallthrough to a shared fallback pool under load.
- Impact: ~3% of US-WEST traffic, elevated p95 and intermittent 502/503 between 08:45–09:25 PDT. No inference results lost.
- Immediate mitigation: scaled fallback capacity and applied a routing-cache patch to prevent repeat fallthroughs.
- Permanent fixes planned: stronger cache priming on deploy paths, an alert for fallthrough rate >0.5%, and a safety throttle on fallback pools when upstream pinning is failing.

Next steps we completed for Novaflow:
1) pushed routing-cache patch to all US clusters (completed 10/27, 09:15 PDT).
2) closed the incident and confirmed stabilization (completed 10/27, 09:25 PDT).
3) opened a follow-up engineering ticket for the permanent fixes (DF-4821).

You can find the one-page summary attached and a fuller postmortem in the shared drive link below. Please let us know if you want a joint review session; we can schedule 30 mins next week to walk your SRE/Platform team through the timeline and planned mitigations.
